newsitem.title: UK: Airbus may cut first A3XX to 470 seats.
newsitem.headline: Airbus may cut first A3XX to 470 seats.

text.p: Europe's Airbus Industrie may scale back the size of the first version of its A3XX superjumbo aircraft from 550 to 470 seats to speed up the launch of the project, a senior industry source said on Friday.

The move would also prompt arch rival Boeing Co to rejoin the race to build the world's first superjumbo, he said. "I think if we go ahead and launch a 470-seat A3XX, and I think the first version will be a 470-seat aircraft, Boeing will come back in," he said.

Boeing recently dropped plans to build a 550-seat version of its 400-seat 747 jumbo jet, currently the world's largest passenger aircraft, saying it could not get enough airlines interested to justify the $7.0 billion cost of the project.

Earlier this month Boeing's chairman and chief executive Phil Condit also denied recent industry speculation that the company was preparing to surprise the market by launching a new large aircraft if Airbus goes ahead with its 550-seat A3XX in two years time.

But Airbus has vowed to press ahead with plans to get the all-new doubledecker aircraft into the air by year 2003 for the same price as an enlarged 747, at around $200 million, at a development cost of $8.0 billion.

Airbus is anxious to break into the large capacity airliner market where Boeing has a monopoly with the 747-400 which Airbus says can also influence an airline's choice of smaller aircraft if it wants fleet commonality.

The Airbus consortium comprises Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
